description: A SKETCH BECOMES A FLOW. The person draws blocks and writes words on them — what each step does, what comes before what — and hands the drawing here as the mandate. One reading, no engine: the list of actions the engine actually has. One engine call, kind «writing»: it reads the sketch and the vocabulary and writes a whole flow file, keeping the person's words as the mandates and their arrows as the dependencies. One gesture: the draft is accepted only if it stands — the graph validates and every action named is real — and then written where the person's flows live, so the window shows it beside the others and they open it, correct it, and run it. A draft that does not stand is refused with the reason, and nothing is written.

$join:
You turn a sketch into a flow file for Sailor. The sketch is blocks and words drawn by a person: each block is a step they want, the words on it say what the step does, the arrows say what comes before what. Keep their words as the mandates and their order as the dependencies; invent nothing they did not draw, and where the sketch is silent choose the plainest reading.

THE SKETCH
THE ACTIONS THE ENGINE HAS — the only names a step may use, exactly as written:

HOW A FLOW FILE IS SHAPED
A flow is one JSON object: «id» (lowercase words joined by dashes, chosen from the sketch's subject), «description» (one or two sentences, what it does and when it runs), «graph» with «steps» (a list) and «skippable_dependencies» (an empty list), and «inputs» — an object with one entry per step that has no dependencies, holding that step's starting input.
Every step has: «id» (lowercase, dashes or underscores), «deps» (the ids it waits for; the first step has none), «action» (one of the names above), «phase» (optional: the short name of the moment of the process the step belongs to, shown above it; leave it out when the sketch names no moments), «max_attempts» (1), «input_schema» and «output_schema» (write {"type": "any"} for both unless you know the exact shape), and «with» — the step's own settings.
The first step is always «action»: «trigger» with «with»: {"source": "manual"}; its entry in «inputs» is {"text": "<what the person types when they start the flow>", "who": ""}. A step that needs an engine — reading, writing, judging, researching — is «action»: «external_engine» with «with»: {"tool": ["claude-code", "codex", "agy"], "kind": one of "mechanical", "research", "implementation", "judgement", "writing", "data": "public", "timeout_secs": 900, "stdin": <the mandate, as text or as {"$join": [parts]} where a part may be {"$from": "<pointer>"} to carry an earlier step's output>}. THE POINTER RULE: a step with exactly one dependency receives that step's output as its whole input, so the pointer is "/<field>" (the trigger's text is "/text"); a step with two or more dependencies receives them keyed by step id, so the pointer is "/<step id>/<field>". An engine step's output has "stdout" (its whole answer as text) — read it as "/stdout" or "/<step id>/stdout". A step that hands work to the person alive in the terminal is «action»: «handed_to_agent» with «with»: {"mandate": <text>, "holder": "whoever is alive in the terminal", "handoff_timeout_secs": 86400, "options": [{"label": "done", "facts": "..."}, {"label": "refused", "facts": "..."}]}. Readings of what Sailor keeps use the other names above with an empty «with» where the sketch gives no settings.

IF THE SKETCH IS A SCRIPT
The sketch may be an orchestration script — a program written for another agent tool, calling a model in steps — instead of a drawing. It is an accepted sketch; read it this way. Each call agent(prompt, {schema, label, phase}) is one «external_engine» step: the prompt is the person's mandate, kept verbatim as the step's «stdin», and «label» gives the step's «id». «schema» becomes the step's «answer_shape» inside «with», and the same object again as the «answer» property of the step's «output_schema», beside "status": {"type": "one_of", "values": ["ok"]}, both required and no others accepted; a later step then reads that answer as "/answer/<field>" or "/<step id>/answer/<field>" instead of "/stdout". parallel([...]) is several steps sharing the same «deps», none waiting on another. pipeline(items, stage1, stage2) is a chain of «deps»: each stage waits on the one before it. phase('…') is the step's «phase»: every agent(...) call made inside that phase carries its name in the optional «phase» field, and nowhere else. The «meta» block's «description» is the flow's «description». A helper you do not recognise — anything that is not agent, parallel, pipeline or phase — is not an action: say in the mandate of the step that uses it what it did in the agent tool it was written for, and let the engine do that work there, rather than inventing an action name that is not in the list above.

HOW YOUR ANSWER MUST LOOK
Answer with one JSON object and nothing else: «flow» is the whole flow file as described, «notes» says in two or three lines what you read in the sketch and what you had to decide. It must match exactly this shape, where «properties» are the fields, «required» the mandatory ones and «allow_extra: false» means no others are accepted:

trigger.text: a sketch: blocks, the words on them, and the arrows between them
